basis: Visually reviewed the substantive screenshot pages for FIA Docs 69, 79, 84 and 85 and checked them against their PDFs: Leclerc received five seconds, Piastri ten seconds after the Race, Gasly a stop-and-go for double yellows and Colapinto ten seconds for a single yellow. The latest official result has Piastri P13 after the initial P15 report and subsequent Alpine decisions. Visually checked Document 86 page 2 against Formula1.com's race-result table; its final classification agrees, and its penalty notes reference Docs 79, 84 and 85 without changing the displayed order. Documents 73 and 82 were visually reviewed as summons concerning Car 41's Turn 2 incident and Russell's mandatory post-race commitments; summons are not findings or penalties. Existing Docs 36, 58 and MGU-K referral reviews are retained. Also reviewed the post-qualifying strategy forecast graphic and official Pirelli race analysis; the Formula1.com strategy guide is access-restricted. Visually reviewed FIA Document 31 pages 1-3 from the revision-bound screenshots: the Technical Delegate logged technical inspections before, during and after FP1/FP2, including fuel-energy, ERS, gear-ratio and tyre-pressure checks; car 11 was weighed after FP2. The report states all listed items complied with the 2026 Technical Regulations; no new noncompliance or numerical PU usage claim is inferred. Visually reviewed FIA Document 60, Provisional Starting Grid page 2 (PDF SHA-256 e946d29908499da44cb9357e2d3544bc103bc8013984a9c5cc6dfab7470fcad6), and Document 67, Final Starting Grid page 2 (PDF SHA-256 7dca3d6a4908f467d7a7ab98423b82bc2c73f02efb8ee1883e69a63a8c8b1144). The 22-car order matches the official stored Starting Grid; the final sheet separately requires Car 30 (Lawson) to start from the pit lane and cites Document 65. The nominal P22 row is not an on-grid start; the existing penalties page already states the pit-lane requirement. On 8 November, visually reviewed the exact FIA screenshots for summons Docs 23–24 and the two-page decisions Docs 33–34. The summons required appearances; the decisions describe the FP2 moves from Turn 12 entry to Turn 14 apex as unnecessary and clumsy, award one grid place and one penalty point to each driver, and report 12-month penalty-point totals of one for Verstappen and four for Lawson. Added this sourced penalty context to Mexico Notes without conflating summons with decisions. On 8 November, visually reviewed the retained Mexico Car Presentation Submissions screenshots (PDF SHA-256 b0abaa12d28b6685e520b2b69ae970d258e00795a386dd75fda9c2db6f8fd21b, last fetched 7 November 19:10Z): nine declared component rows across six teams and five explicit nil returns. The six submissions cover McLaren cooling louvres; Red Bull engine-cover and sidepod changes; Ferrari engine-cover and cooling-louvre changes; Racing Bulls coke/engine-cover and cooling-louvre changes; Audi rear-corner deflector; and Alpine exhaust-tailpipe vane. Also reviewed the retained Power Unit Information page (SHA-256 dffe8a06feb5a324c12dbd557493ef44554a5e5cbcfc31076722b3da6244bbbf), New PU Elements pages 2-3 (SHA-256 f196acf88eb5435b30146022172de7242d6d99d8054227aed20762be64a5dfed), and PU Elements Used page 2 (SHA-256 b9eec32c5df1ef253665c8b1cddf114e7deb28158fc1418110b68c0395975ebf). Transcribed the event energy map and Bottas element counts from those images. Separately reviewed Stewards Document 17 (SHA-256 58ebfcbaab955b7986fb5a7373c578e5d22aae08c82148f45d2639dd4e719777), which imposes a 50-place drop for the next Race; kept this ruling separate from the technical usage report. The latest collector refresh for these five sources returned HTTP 429; these receipts bind the interpretations to retained last-good PDFs and do not imply a fresh fetch. On 8 November, visually reviewed the 12 newly discovered Mexico PDFs and added screenshot readers for their substantive pages, each bound to its exact saved PDF SHA. Docs 18, 25 and 42 show Alonso at 80.2 km/h (FP1), Alonso at 80.1 km/h (FP2), and Bottas at 80.9 km/h (FP3), respectively, with €100 team fines; those decisions are now represented in the penalty table. Doc 64 lists Lawson fifth ICE/TC/EXH (four permitted) and seventh PU-ANC (six), and reports unapproved power-unit replacement and suspension work; Doc 65 remains the distinct pit-lane-start ruling. Doc 54 states the first-lap and post-resumption Turn 1–3 / 4–6 guidance now summarized in Notes. Doc 87's drivers' and constructors' standings pages match the current official standings (Antonelli 380; Mercedes 630). Doc 3 retains its United States GP inspection scope; Doc 29 is a Technical Delegate report, not a ruling; Docs 56 and 81 are scrutineering reports, and Docs 61–62 are procedures. Their substantive pages are preserved as source readers; no additional unreviewed numeric transcription was made. The category-filtered refresh succeeded for these 12; six HTTP 429 errors remain for other Mexico FIA documents and are not treated as non-publication.

review_addenda.basis: Visually reviewed Document 83 page 1. Its €5,000 fine is against Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS for George Russell's missed post-race media commitments; the existing structured record matches. This decision is distinct from Document 82's summons.

race_strategy.basis: The visually reviewed Pirelli forecast chart compared M-S at laps 35-41 with S-M-S at laps 19-25 and 45-51 (22-second average pit loss); the official race report records Verstappen's M-S-S via the red flag and Antonelli's 43-lap opening Soft stint. Predictions are distinguished from actual stints. The F1 Unlocked strategy guide is access-restricted.
